meta.title: Evaluating Comprehensive State Tobacco Prevention and Control Programs Using an Outcome Indicator Framework
meta.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; RTI International

brief.intended_change: Prevent tobacco use initiation among young people and reduce tobacco-related disease, disability, and deaths.
brief.population: Young people, including youth and young adults.
brief.place: United States, through state and territorial tobacco prevention and control programs.
brief.time_horizon: No fixed intervention or follow-up period is specified; the framework distinguishes short-, intermediate-, and long-term outcomes.
brief.intervention: Comprehensive state tobacco prevention and control programs, typically led by state and territorial health departments, supported by National Tobacco Control Program funding and technical assistance and other revenue streams. No standardized dosage is specified.
brief.context: Nearly all tobacco use begins during youth and young adulthood. State programs operate in varying local contexts and receive funding from sources including tobacco taxes and Master Settlement Agreement payments.
brief.outcome_first: Develop a theory of change for preventing tobacco use initiation among young people in the United States. Show how this could contribute to reducing tobacco-related disease, disability, and deaths across different state and territorial contexts.
brief.intervention_first: Develop a theory of change for comprehensive state and territorial tobacco prevention and control programs in the United States. Focus on their aim of preventing tobacco use initiation among young people and reducing subsequent tobacco-related health harms.

verdict.raw: Many state programs have reported use of the outcome indicator framework to guide not only their evaluation planning but also their strategic planning. This indicator has the highest ratings across all indicator selection criteria and is measured in an existing, ongoing national survey that provides state-level estimates. Although the outcome indicator framework has numerous strengths, it also has limitations. As developed by OSH, the outcome indicator framework does not provide infrastructure or process indicators.
verdict.quote: Many state programs have reported use of the outcome indicator framework to guide not only their evaluation planning but also their strategic planning
studies: California Department of Public Health & California Tobacco Control Program 2016

conclusions.summary: This article presents an evidence-informed, prospective evaluation framework, not a test of the complete causal model. It argues that the framework helps tobacco control programs plan theory-driven evaluations, focus priorities, and align work with national goals. Indiana used it to update strategic objectives, including e-cigarette indicators; California incorporated the approach into local planning and evaluation, and a related approach was used in nutrition, physical activity, and obesity prevention. Limitations include absent infrastructure and process indicators, non-exhaustive outcome indicators, gaps in local and subgroup surveillance, and limited measurement of tobacco industry influence. The article does not rank causal links or report link-level evidence verdicts.
recommendations: Select outcome pathways and indicators collaboratively with stakeholders, taking account of community context, program timelines, and resources.
Complement outcome indicators with descriptive information on program infrastructure, activities, and outputs.
Add, modify, or further operationalize indicators to fit program context and evaluation needs.
Check whether surveillance provides sufficiently timely, precise geographic and subpopulation estimates; supplement data collection when necessary.
Continue updating the framework for emerging tobacco products, innovative practices, and tobacco-related disparities.
Develop stronger guidance for identifying populations experiencing disparities and monitoring their outcomes.
Use the framework with rigorous evaluation and the CDC Framework for Program Evaluation.

open_questions: The source has no causal-link ratings or evaluation results for the complete model. Indicator ratings concern six selection criteria, including strength of evaluation evidence; their scale words and detailed scores are not supplied here. No indicator rating has been converted into a link verdict.
Short-term, Intermediate, and Long-term columns are mapped respectively to outcome_short, outcome_long, and impact because the fixed schema has no intermediate-outcome layer.
The activity boxes feed a shared connector leading to the five output arrows; they are represented as a container rather than as all possible individual activity-to-output links.
The output brace is represented as a container with arrows to the four short-term outcomes.

Several connectors overlap or run close to boxes. In particular, links l_12–l_15 and l_19 should be checked against a higher-resolution original; their traced endpoints are recorded with medium confidence.
The rightmost connector is read as branching from outcome 9 to outcomes 10, 11, and 12. Its routes pass behind or alongside the intervening boxes.
No clearly visible arrow connects the infrastructure input box to the activity boxes; none has been added.

The bottom 'Focus on reducing tobacco-related disparities' band is treated as cross-cutting context, not a separate result box. The thin line and small central mark above it do not establish a clear causal arrow endpoint in the supplied rendering.
The text supports the morbidity and mortality portion of k_10 but does not separately judge whether disparities were reduced.

The indicator example says on page 5 that an existing national survey provides state-level estimates, while page 6 says NYTS does not provide state-level estimates. The manuscript does not resolve that discrepancy.
Figure 2 is an example indicator profile, not another theory-of-change diagram. Its image was not supplied, so detailed indicator evidence and ratings cannot be transcribed.
The article provides no fixed program dosage or evaluation horizon. The exact manuscript URL and reuse licence were not supplied.
